      "title": "Integration.DoesNotExist path skips the new installer identity check",
      "body": "GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() when no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id. The github_authenticated_user comparison is only performed later for an existing active Integration. If the webhook has not yet created the Integration, failed, or the row was deleted, the pipeline completes and build_integration will create/link the installation using only the user-supplied installation_id. That bypasses the PR's stated validation that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches the installer, potentially allowing a user to bind a GitHub installation they did not install if they know or guess its installation_id. The flow should fail closed, or wait until sender metadata is available, when the installer cannot be verified."

      "body": "The mismatch check assumes integration.metadata contains a 'sender' dict with a 'login' key. Integrations created before this change, created through the Integration.DoesNotExist path, or created from webhook payloads lacking sender will not have this key. In those cases the request raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the controlled installation-failed page, and users may be unable to install or reinstall. Use a safe lookup and reject the installation when sender/login is absent."

If another integration provider has the same external_id, the code can fetch the wrong Integration, produce incorrect 'installed on another organization' errors, apply the sender check to the wrong record, or raise MultipleObjectsReturned. Filter these queries by GitHubIntegrationProvider.key."
    },

A request with an invalid state value can therefore still mutate pipeline state. Since this is a GET pipeline endpoint and installation_id later controls which GitHub installation is linked, validating state before binding, or not binding installation_id when state is present, would avoid unnecessary state tampering."

OAuth servers use redirect_uri at the token endpoint to enforce that the code was issued for the expected callback URL. If the GitHub OAuth app ever has multiple callback URLs, omitting it weakens protection against authorization-code injection. Include the same redirect_uri in the token request."

findings.title: Integration.DoesNotExist path skips the new installer identity check
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() when no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id. The github_authenticated_user comparison is only performed later for an existing active Integration. If the webhook has not yet created the Integration, failed, or the row was deleted, the pipeline completes and build_integration will create/link the installation using only the user-supplied installation_id. That bypasses the PR's stated validation that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches the installer, potentially allowing a user to bind a GitHub installation they did not install if they know or guess its installation_id. The flow should fail closed, or wait until sender metadata is available, when the installer cannot be verified.

findings.title: Unsafe access to metadata['sender']['login'] can 500
findings.body: The mismatch check assumes integration.metadata contains a 'sender' dict with a 'login' key. Integrations created before this change, created through the Integration.DoesNotExist path, or created from webhook payloads lacking sender will not have this key. In those cases the request raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the controlled installation-failed page, and users may be unable to install or reinstall. Use a safe lookup and reject the installation when sender/login is absent.

findings.title: Integration lookups do not filter by provider
findings.body: Both Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) at line 478 and the later get at line 494 omit provider='github'. If another integration provider has the same external_id, the code can fetch the wrong Integration, produce incorrect 'installed on another organization' errors, apply the sender check to the wrong record, or raise MultipleObjectsReturned. Filter these queries by GitHubIntegrationProvider.key.

findings.title: installation_id is bound before OAuth state is validated
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch binds installation_id into pipeline state before checking request.GET['state'] against pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid state value can therefore still mutate pipeline state. Since this is a GET pipeline endpoint and installation_id later controls which GitHub installation is linked, validating state before binding, or not binding installation_id when state is present, would avoid unnecessary state tampering.

findings.title: OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri
findings.body: The authorize redirect includes redirect_uri, but the access-token exchange created at lines 416-420 does not send it. OAuth servers use redirect_uri at the token endpoint to enforce that the code was issued for the expected callback URL. If the GitHub OAuth app ever has multiple callback URLs, omitting it weakens protection against authorization-code injection. Include the same redirect_uri in the token request.

findings.title: Network/API failures in OAuth exchange are unhandled
findings.body: safe_urlopen and get_user_info can raise exceptions for network failures or GitHub API errors, but only the response body parsing is wrapped in try/except. A transient failure during installation will produce a 500 instead of the intended installation-failed error page. Catch the expected HTTP/API exceptions and return error().

findings.title: Empty installation_id is treated as present
findings.body: installation_id = request.GET.get('installation_id', pipeline.fetch_state(...)) followed by 'if installation_id is None' accepts an empty string from ?installation_id=. The code then binds '' and queries or requests GitHub with an empty installation id, causing avoidable errors. Treat empty or whitespace-only values as missing and redirect to the app URL.

findings.title: No tests for missing sender metadata or missing Integration path
findings.body: The added tests cover the happy path and a mismatch when metadata.sender exists, but not the cases where Integration exists without metadata.sender/login or where Integration.DoesNotExist causes the pipeline to continue. Those paths can raise KeyError or bypass the new security check, so they need regression tests.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found does not exercise installation lookup
findings.body: The test sends a state value that does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-request error before reaching the mocked 404 for /app/installations/{installation_id}. The assertion therefore does not verify the intended installation-not-found behavior. Use a valid pipeline state and complete the OAuth step to test the 404 path.
